name: Jin Zhang
forbes_bio: Zhang Jin chairs Guangdong-headquartered Cedar Holdings, whose business interests include real estate, finance and auto sales.
Born the son of a government worker, Zhang first prospered from stock investments.
Zhang Jin is a graduate of Shenzhen University.

name: Patrizio Vinciarelli
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Patrizio Vinciarelli founded Vicor Corp in 1981 and is the president, CEO and chairman of the company.
Vicor, based in Andover, Massachusetts, designs, develops and manufactures power components such as AC-DC converters.
Before starting Vicor, Vinciarelli studied high-energy physics at CERN in Switzerland and the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey.
He has a PhD in physics from the University of Rome and holds more than 150 patents related to electronics conversion technology.

name: Alberto Palatchi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Alberto Palatchi transformed a store he inherited from his parents in 1964 into Pronovias, one of the largest wedding dress companies in the world.
In 2017, Palatchi sold 90% of Pronovias to British private equity firm BC Partners for an estimated $550 million.
Pronovias wedding dresses are sold in more than 105 countries through a network of 123 stores and more than 4,000 points of sale.
Palatchi also has more than $1.1 billion invested in a Spanish investment fund that is similar to a mutual fund.
He's also invested in art and a broad swath of U.S. and European stocks.
forbes_facts: Palatchi's father fled Turkey during World War I and moved to Barcelona.
In 1922 Palatchi's parents opened a store in Barcelona called El Suizo that sold lace and embroidery for wedding dresses.

name: Rajan Raheja
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2021)
forbes_bio: Low-profile Rajan Raheja hails from the sprawling Raheja property clan in Mumbai.
After a family split he went on to build a separate diversified empire that includes interests in cement, batteries and cable television.
Raheja's biggest asset is listed auto battery maker Exide Industries.
He also owns listed cable television unit Hathway Cable Datacom, in which Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries has a majority stake.
His son, Akshay Raheja, sits on the board of Raheja QBE General Insurance, a joint venture between his listed Prism Johnson and Australia's QBE Insurance.

name: C.C. Leung
forbes_bio: C.C. Leung is the vice chairman and president of Quanta Computer, the world's largest contract manufacturer of laptops by sales volume.
He cofounded Quanta with Barry Lam, also a billionaire, in 1988.
The company also makes other electronic devices and is one of the world's top server suppliers to cloud service providers by revenue, counting Meta and Google among its clients.
Leung's daughters, Amy, Annie and Anita, run Taipei's shopping mall Bellavita.

name: Luca Garavoglia
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Luca Garavoglia is chairman of Campari Group, one of the world's largest alcoholic beverage companies.
Campari's brands includes Skyy Vodka, Wild Turkey, Aperol and Campari.
Garavoglia inherited his stake in the company from his parents. His mother, Rosa Anna Magno Garavoglia, died in 2016.
He now owns an estimated 26% of the company, which listed on the Milan Stock Exchange in 2001.
His late father, Domenico, was a long-time employee before the last remaining heir of the Campari family passed the company to him.
forbes_facts: His Campari group reportedly sold a villa on the French riviera to fellow billionaire Rinat Akhmetov in January 2020 for 200 million euros.
Garavoglia speaks Italian, English, French and Spanish.

name: Yoo Jung-hyun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Yoo Jung-hyun owns a minority stake in online gaming giant Nexon through NXC.
Her husband Kim Jung-ju built up Nexon and then retired from management in 2006; he died in 2022 at age 54.
She joined NXC in 1995 and became its chairman in 2024.
forbes_facts: Yoo Jung-hyun met her future husband at a ski resort when he was a freshman.

name: Kathy Britton
forbes_bio: Kathy Britton runs Houston-based homebuilder Perry Homes.
Her father, Bob Perry (d. 2013), founded the company in 1967 and built it into one of Texas' biggest builders.
She took over as CEO in 2013 and expanded Perry Homes in places like Austin, Dallas, Fort Worth and Florida.
She's now executive chair of the $2.4 billion (sales) business, which has built more than 65,000 homes across more than 120 communities.
forbes_facts: Britton worked in Perry Homes? sales and land acquisition departments before becoming CEO.

name: Yang Huiyan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2017-2025); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Yang Huiyan chairs property developer Country Garden. She became the only one at the helm after her father Yeung Kwok Keung stepped down as co-chair in February 2023.
Yang has long been groomed for succession. Yeung transferred a 57% Country Garden stake to her back in 2007, which once made her the world's youngest female billionaire.
Her sister Yang Ziying also sits on the board; husband Chen Chong is a non-executive director.
In August 2023, Country Garden triggered fresh turmoil in China's beleaguered real estate market after it missed interest payments of $22.5 million on two offshore bonds.
Yang donated in the same year $826 million worth of shares in property management arm Country Garden Services to a Hong Kong charity set up by sister Ziying.
forbes_facts: Yang obtained a bachelor's degree from Ohio State University.

name: Cho Hyun-joon
forbes_bio: Cho Hyun-joon is the chairman of Hyosung Group, whose interests include textiles, chemicals and construction.
He is the eldest son of the late former chairman Cho Seok-rae, who stepped down in 2016 and passed away in 2024.
Cho worked at Mitsubishi International and Morgan Stanley before joining Hyosung.
He was sentenced to two years in prison in 2019 for embezzlement; he appealed the conviction. Cho's sentencing was suspended for three years, allowing him to continue running Hyosung.
forbes_facts: Cho's uncle is Hankook Tire honorary chairman Cho Yang-Rai.

name: Vivek Ramaswamy
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Wikidata (2023); SEC insider holdings (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Vivek Ramaswamy is a biotech entrepreneur, author and Republican politician who ran for president in 2024.
A Harvard and Yale Law graduate, Ramaswamy began his career on Wall Street trading biotech stocks for the hedge fund QVT.
In 2015, he took public a speculative Alzheimer's drug (which later failed) in a $3 billion IPO that formed the basis of Roivant Sciences, a drug discovery and investment firm.

In the years since, Roivant has helped bring multiple successful drug candidates to market; positive Phase 3 trial results for brepocitinib, which targets an autoimmune disease, sent its stock soaring in late 2025.
Ramaswamy left Roivant in 2020 to write Woke, Inc., a best seller, and found Strive, an asset manager that provides anti-woke investment funds.
Ramaswamy helped Elon Musk found DOGE as its co-head, but departed after a few weeks amid reports of butting heads with Musk.
forbes_facts: Ramaswamy graduated as valedictorian from St. Xavier High School in Cincinnati, Ohio.

name: Basudeo Singh
forbes_bio: Basudeo Singh is the executive chairman of Indian generics firm Alkem Laboratories.
The company has 18 factories including one in California to make pharmaceutical ingredients.
Basudeo Singh is the cousin of Alkem's late billionaire cofounder Samprada Singh.
His son Dhananjay Kumar Singh, Alkem's joint managing director, who was named to succeed him as executive chairman, passed away in 2021.

name: Ilkka Herlin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Ilkka Herlin is the great-grandson of famed Finnish business leader Harald Herlin, who invested in Kone Elevators in 1924.
After his father's death in 2003, Ilkka and his siblings discovered the will had been rewritten leaving most of the ownership in Kone to their brother Antti.
Angered that they had never been informed, the siblings battled for control. The dispute ended in 2005, with Kone being split in two.
Antti maintained control over the elevator business while his siblings were given stakes in Cargotec, producer of machinery for heavy duty ship cargo.
Niklas, one of the sibling, passed away in 2017. Three of the siblings are billionaires.
forbes_facts: Ilkka Herling has a PhD in History from the University of Helsingfors.
He is one of the founders of Baltic Sea Action Group, a trust for the conservation of the Baltic Sea, and is involved in a carbon capture technology project.

name: PJ Hyett
forbes_bio: PJ Hyett cofounded software development platform GitHub in 2008.
A decade later, over 28 million developer were using the platform.
Microsoft bought GitHub for $7.5 billion in 2018.
